title: Legacy ~/.dd and ~/.supermem home-dir stores verified stale and deleted
body:
Before deleting a legacy home-dir store, open its sqlite (memory_atoms table) read-only and diff its topic_keys/lifecycle_state against the current project's .dd/atoms/ git-truth. If every topic_key already exists there as active (candidates included, since they may have since been reviewed under the same topic_key), the legacy dir holds nothing unmigrated and rm -rf is safe. This is the concrete check for roadmap Gap 6 (data-directory rename orphaning telemetry) when the orphaned copy is suspected empty of unique data.

Why: Ran this exact check on 2026-09-19: ~/.supermem/supermem/index.sqlite (17 active memory_atoms) and ~/.dd/supermem-3892c3ad040f/index.sqlite (17 active + 4 candidate) both had 100% topic_key overlap with .dd/atoms/ in this repo -- the 4 old candidates (dd/lifecycle/automatic-transitions-and-review, dd/telemetry/bridge-interception, dd/testing/backdated-created-at, dd/store/data-directory-renames) are now active under identical topic_keys in the current store. Confirmed nothing unique, deleted both dirs with user confirmation.

evidence.ref: node --sqlite query of C:/Users/walle/.dd/supermem-3892c3ad040f/index.sqlite and C:/Users/walle/.supermem/supermem/index.sqlite memory_atoms tables
evidence.summary: Listed topic_key + lifecycle_state from both legacy sqlite files; all 17+17 active and 4 candidate topic_keys matched entries already present and active in this repo's .dd/atoms/
User explicitly approved deleting ~/.dd and ~/.supermem after the verification was shown

v1.trigger: When deciding whether to delete a pre-rename legacy data directory (~/.supermem, ~/.dd/<project-hash>) left over from before the project moved to per-project .dd/local
